summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests silevertinib, an oral EGFR inhibitor, combined with temozolomide in people with newly diagnosed glioblastoma. Silevertinib is taken by mouth once daily with temozolomide on days 1 to 5 of each 28-day cycle; silevertinib continues until disease progression, and temozolomide is given for a maximum of 6 cycles. The study measures whether participants live longer without disease progression compared with temozolomide alone, as stated in the brief summary; a separate primary outcome measure is not stated.
summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa silevertinib, un inhibidor oral de EGFR, combinado con temozolomida en personas con glioblastoma de diagnóstico reciente. Silevertinib se toma por vía oral una vez al día junto con temozolomida los días 1 a 5 de cada ciclo de 28 días; silevertinib continúa hasta la progresión de la enfermedad, y la temozolomida se administra por un máximo de 6 ciclos. El estudio mide si los participantes viven más tiempo sin progresión de la enfermedad en comparación con la temozolomida sola, según se indica en el resumen breve; un desenlace primario separado no se indica.
who_for: Newly diagnosed glioblastoma that is IDH wild type, confirmed by tissue examination
Positive EGFR status in the brain tumor; EGFRvIII and unmethylated MGMT promoter required for Part 2
Surgery followed by standard radiation (54 to 60 Gy) and temozolomide, with no other treatment for newly diagnosed GBM
At least 4 weeks since radiation ended, with a post-radiation MRI showing no progression
not_for: Recurrent multifocal, metastatic, leptomeningeal, or extracranial GBM, or gliomatosis cerebri
Progression of GBM before enrollment, screening, or randomization, or biopsy-only without resectional surgery
Prior or planned treatment for GBM with an EGFR-targeting agent, bevacizumab, chemotherapy, immunotherapy, experimental therapy, or intratumoral therapy
Intent to use Optune (TTF), significant uncontrolled health conditions, or other malignancies
